| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) | An endorsement scheme can deny each operator control over its own authority and still reward it for delegating, because the authority an operator holds and how far its preferred policies are realized are different quantities | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. A2 made it precise. Two conditions are imposed: each operator's own authority is insensitive to its own endorsements, and its payoff is how closely the collective decision matches what it would endorse. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-286](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) | Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed | A7's central thesis, the explanatory half of the manuscript, kept apart from the constitutive half ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)) as A7 itself asked. Its novelty is the unification, not any ingredient: "multi-agent cognition, competing control systems, temporal discounting, self-exciting processes, and organizational emergence all have substantial literatures". It is the claim [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) objects to. It does not say these processes are a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) v2 | What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation | A6 §7 and A10 §4.3. A6 separated activation continuity, organizational continuity and policy continuity, and put identity in the second: "A dormant coalition can remain available for reactivation because learned parameters, memory traces, and endorsement structures persist." A10 added that continuity of descent "is not automatically an equivalence relation. Organizational histories can branch, merge, and partially overlap." It sits beside [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md), which asks for a coherence measure conserved along a system's own trajectory, and qualifies it for gaps. Its second half is Parfit's branching argument (THEORY-447) applied to organizational continuity. It uses [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s persisting sense. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v2 | A simulation whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed cannot show self-constitution, because the norms the organization appears to maintain are then the modeller's, not set by the organization itself | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. The objection undermines the evidence route; it does not refute the thesis. It is answered if the operators' objectives are themselves produced and revised by the organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-296](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) | What a system has, what it knows it has, and what it can deploy within a task's deadline are different, and the last is a relation among the resource, the agent, its environment, the task, the deadline and the cue, not a property of any one of them | A18's first candidate, from the owner's EMT case ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)): the drug was stocked, the EMT knew it, and it could not be found before the medic moved on. "If I can't find it, it isn't there" is false of the inventory and right of the decision. [TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md) names the relation. A19 added the cue: the same memory under a different request may retrieve it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) | When an operator's authority is updated by how well it performs on the interpretation it helped make dominant, the coupled meaning and influence of an organization can amplify an initial interpretive advantage without any gain in fidelity to independent evidence | A22's narrow claim and A23 VIII.E's central hypothesis, from the owner's U22: connect retrieval-mediated anchoring to the record's distributed agent as dual meaning and influence canvases ([CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md), [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)). An existence hypothesis until a model ([CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md)) is analysed. If the influence field adds nothing to ordinary adaptive retrieval, [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) stands against it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) | Under a deadline, search can establish presence by finding one item but absence only by exhausting the collection, so "If I can't find it, it isn't there" acts on an unfinished search as negation as failure acts on a finished one: a default stronger than either the closed-world assumption or negation as failure, safe only when the arrangement makes the full search finish within the deadline | The medic's "If I can't find it, it isn't there" ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)) and the owner's "if I can't find it quickly enough, it may as well not be there" ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) act on a failed search as if it showed absence. One find shows presence, but absence needs a check of everything, which a deadline forbids. First filed as negation as failure on a time bound, with Reiter and Clark unread. Both readings corrected it. The two assumptions are separate. Reiter's closed-world assumption is that the database is complete about the world. Clark's negation as failure is licensed only by finite failure: "the exhaustive but unsuccessful search for a proof". A search cut off by a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It assumes a closed world and that the unsearched part would have failed. It is safe when the full pass finishes in time. In [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the EMT knew the drug was stocked, which is exactly where Reiter shows the closed-world assumption inconsistent. So there it was a decision to stop, not an inference. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) |
| [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) says when a distinction is real enough to name. Its evidence grows with the number of copies. The parable says when a distinction must be built to act in time: a single brick among similar ones. Expected search falls as copies grow. The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) v2 | Sorting schemes over objects with determinate properties never conflict as descriptions, since the product of any sortings refines them all; they conflict as arrangements, since a fixed number of bins realizes one partition when each item is stored once, and which costs least depends on what is searched for and on what stands out within a bin | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |
| [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) | A search cut off before an exhaustive pass can establish absence when the arrangement certifies that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item: a sorted table answers non-membership in a logarithmic number of probes, and the Threshold Algorithm stops early with its answer proved, so absence needs a certificate about the remainder, not exhaustion; similarity search in high dimension is where no such certificate exists | Filed at the owner's request, from the database readings set against [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry: presence by one find, absence "only by exhausting the collection". Sorted order and the Threshold Algorithm each establish absence from part of the collection, because the arrangement bounds what the rest can hold. That meets [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s own defeat condition, and the claim is conceded: [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) restates it. Where the arrangement gives no bound, as in similarity search in high dimension, [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry stands. | Active |
| [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" asserts operational unavailability, that the item will not be put to use before the deadline, not absence: a search that fails by the deadline establishes unavailability outright, and licenses absence only with a certificate that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item, from exhaustion, from an invariant of the arrangement, or from a closed-world default | Restates [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) at the owner's request, after [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) showed that absence can be established without exhausting a collection. The owner's own wording in [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md), "it may as well not be there", is hyperbole for operational availability ([TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md)), not a claim about inventory. Read so, the rule reports an outcome and needs no default. [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s analysis survives as the account of the literal reading: what a failed search must be joined with before it licenses absence. The gap between the two readings is [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s Bayes term, and it matters when the statement is passed to someone who will act on presence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | A fixed number of bins realizes one partition only when each item is stored once: with copies, overlapping partitions coexist, as hashing-based similarity search stores each item in many partitions and pays for it in space, so sortings conflict as arrangements only under a one-copy constraint, which binds bricks but not index entries | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time". That holds when each item is in one place. An index can hold many copies, and hashing-based similarity indexes do exactly that, trading the space of the copies against query time on an exact curve. It narrows [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) to collections whose items cannot be copied, which includes the LEGO case; it does not touch the claim about descriptions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-316](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-316.md) | A person's drive profile is time-indexed: who drives changes with state, such as hungry or sated and stressed or calm, with task and with regime | Split from [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the first of the owner's two parts of 2026-10-11, "'who drives' isn't a constant", stated on its own. It is argued from the drive-profile term and the will line's account of which regime is effective, and no observation the record holds estimates a person's drive profile over successive windows, so it is interpretive. The microbiome part, which the reviews support, stays in [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-317](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) v2 | Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide | Split from [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical half of that claim, the sociology of audiences on which its sheaf reading rests. Its evidence is boyd (2008, read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md)), after Meyrowitz (1985), and one documented collapse, [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md). boyd's claims about collapse are documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the Carmichael case reaches the record secondhand, so it stays Proposed. It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). Three stages: an observer finds a stable statistic of fast interactions; members recognize it and use it; their use preserves or regenerates it. Only the third makes the variable an endogenous level. It is the general form of [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md), where trust is the temporal regularity of endorsement that then steers endorsement. It does not say that such a variable individuates one collective: five slow variables sharing a referent may be five processes. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-328](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-328.md) | When the continuities that ordinarily come bundled in a collective (legal franchise, civic role, interpersonal transmission, narrative and place) are separated, several later collectives can each be a genuine successor of the earlier one in a different respect, without any of them, or the earlier collective, having branched in numerical identity | A4's H5 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, in its weak form, on the Washington Senators. The league's successor to the original club is the Twins; the city's is the expansion Senators; the city's present team claims its history through place and narrative. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-118](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-118.md) at the owner's word. It concerns plural successor relations, not branching identity, and rests on one documented case with no data on how supporters divided. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). A5: "a system's ability to reproduce itself as the same kind is not automatically sufficient for its numerical persistence as the same individual." The second time the record meets "causal-organizational continuity": [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) noted A10 §4.3's of 2026-10-13 and did not file it. It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v2 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects." A8 took it and qualified it: a market can crash and a stadium can chant in seconds, so timescale is "a facet of organizational level, not ... an ordering that must hold in every case". Simon's near-decomposability already ties weak coupling between blocks to slow aggregate dynamics ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)). The claim does not say that a slow variable is thereby a level, a system or an individual. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-332](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md) | A loosely organized population can change what an outside institution does through its members' separately motivated acts of making, selecting and passing things on, without forming a collective intention or judgment, when the organized pattern of those acts, and not only the acts of identifiable individuals, earns its place in explaining the change | A7's "distributed cultural uptake", of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on the owner's Juggernaut case. On A7's ladder (aggregate behaviour, amplification, collective causal efficacy, collective intention, corporate agency) it asserts the third rung and denies that the third needs the fourth. Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) at the owner's word, with A7's defeater priced by [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), which A7 said it needed. It does not say the fandom was the efficacious unit. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The mapping is the assistant's, A6, filed at the owner's request ("address the still open stuff"). At U8 the owner endorsed it as filed ("Yes, as filed"). It reads both lines into [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s operator model. The sharp edge: it says the lines share one model, not that either line's results transfer to the other unchanged. Each mapping is a hypothesis until a result on one line is shown to hold, through it, on the other. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-339](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to endorsement has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? No. The coupling γ is 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄), where κ̄ is how far the shared meaning bends the committed predictions and κ′ how far it bends the reading of the evidence. It is corrective, null or capturing as κ′ is below, at or above κ̄. Strong correction can fail by oscillation when \|βγ\| ≥ 1 − αδ. Revising predictions after the evidence sets γ = 0 but also stops authority from tracking who predicts well. Linear, at the symmetric state, for squared-error scoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-341](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The claim is stated in that model's terms, as [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and in the diachronic form A4 proposed and the owner asked to be filed at U5 ("make the revisions"): a judgement need not produce the observation it judges, but it reshapes the observer that produces the next one. The sharp edge: the synchronic form, in which each judgement produces its own outcome, is not claimed. That is the open route of [TERM-039](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-039.md) and [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md), and the record demoted it once before ([CLAIM-109](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-109.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) | What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available | The assistant's synthesis, A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, filed at the owner's request at U5. Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. The claim does not say action is unimportant, only that it is not what does the anchoring. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-344](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md) | Resolve is a maintained organization of precedence, commitment and revision that keeps a temporally extended policy effective across changes in locally dominant evaluations while keeping the capacity to revise it; mere slowness or persistence is not resolve | The owner's frame, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "I think emergence of "resolve" could be an interesting frame within which to examine our will-organization framework." A37 defined it, and A39 to A47 revised it each turn: retention and revision as separate grades, fragility against rigidity (A41), access against authority (A42), and governance that makes its own repeated exercise unnecessary (A45, A47). The record already holds a theory of resolve, Ainslie's recursive staking of future choices ([THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)); this is its organizational and revisable form, placed in [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md)'s will-organization cell. The sharp edge: the standard for when revision is warranted is not supplied, and is [QUESTION-087](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md)'s open problem. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md) | Feasibility, aggregation and epistemic coordination are independent obstructions to an organization's realizing its demands: each can occur with the other two absent | Owner-seeded, U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: Arrow's theorem, then cryptography and "the two generals problem". A36 placed them: "Arrow's theorem belongs in the theory of endorsement, not directly in the geometry of feasible updates", and the two generals add "epistemic frustration". Three elementary constructions, each with one obstruction and not the others, are given in the body. The sharp edge: the independence is relative to fixing the demands as the constituents' own acceptance conditions; that no remedy for one removes another is A36's further reading, argued in the body and not part of the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v2 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) | No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified by the description that preserves it | A21 §18's Candidate 2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, with A21 §5's clause against circularity and A22's Construction C ([CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md)). A21: "no coarse-graining may be treated as generally normatively adequate solely because it preserves organizational stability, predictive accuracy, or aggregate performance." The case is demonstrated: total output preserves an institution's every judgment and merges a member's claim. The general conclusion is interpretive. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s target-relativity carried from individuation to evaluation, and [CLAIM-060](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-060.md) in the language of coarse-graining. Filed in distributed-agency because its case is a whole against its members. The sharp edge: it does not say which target is right, and it denies that the description can settle it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. In general a vanishing positive combination of gradients is either every gradient zero or a certificate that no update improves them all, and the scalar cannot tell which. The sharp edge: it is a fact about a weighted sum, not about what a monitor reading it represents. A29's "the unity of the distress signal need not arise from the unity of the underlying causes" is the interpretive reading, kept apart in the body. | Active |
| [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v2 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility are not the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. Positive governance regret establishes excess worst-case shortfall relative to the optimum, and can hold while every requirement is met. Neither quantity identifies an obstructing mechanism, a governance failure or active thwarting; governance-induced frustration needs an argument or intervention showing the allocation of influence responsible. A35: "Importantly, these dual multipliers are not endorsement weights." | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" A41's answer, condensed: an insider can aim at the organization's future allocation of authority rather than at the present decision, so robustness must protect the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, and the same protection can silence the opposition that corrects the organization, though some safeguards protect both. Insider threats and internal opposition can look alike. The sharp edge: Byzantine fault tolerance protects a fixed specification; this claim is about protecting the capacity to change it, which no protocol of that kind supplies. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". Worked out by A38 and restated by A39 §2B and A43. Relief, as enlargement of the compatibility complex ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), is judged over a fixed reference set of demands, for an organization identified before and after, under a stated correspondence. Watson's comparison ([THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md)) is already relative to a decomposition; what this adds is the comparison across time, when the decomposition itself changes. The sharp edge: it does not say transformation is worse than relief, only that it answers a different question. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). A31 granted it: "applying individuation first, then volition, then affect exposes a problem in our previous discussion". Individuated for the training dynamics, the unit is at least the network–optimizer pair; mapped through the six relations of will-organization, most of the governance of updates is outside the network's jurisdiction. So optimization difficulty in conventional training is real and belongs to the training system. The sharp edge: it does not say the governance is unreal, or that a network cannot come to hold some of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) v2 | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either | The owner's, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe we should focus less on distress and more on frustration". A33 granted it: "Frustration is the most promising theoretical primitive of the three." Frustration is a fact about demands, admissible transformations and governance, so it can be stated without feelings and without a common scale. It supersedes in substance the distress-first formulations of A28–A32, which were never filed. The sharp edge: it says what to start from, not that a frustrated organization is distressed or feels anything. The claim bears on the organizational-affect line, which is Deferred ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md)); whether that line reopens is the owner's decision, not made here. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |
